note: A positioning question, raised by the operator: take the human-facing language-translation part out, or make it an add-on. This records the shape of the answer and the boundary, so a later build has a decided line to work to. Grounded in a scout of the tree, not a guess: the pivot §4.1/§4.2 named ('the category is AI verification, not translation memory') is already largely done at the surface -- the README leads with the covenant and sealed/draft, the onboarding wizard is decision-framed (DOMAIN='decision'), and the demos are decision scenarios (big_jim.py is a car-lot 'runs great' claim, not a phrase pair). What is still translation-shaped and human-facing is narrow: the desk's default domain is still ('en','es') (nestor/ui.py:234-235) and the translate recipe is still offered as a peer rather than an opt-in. Proposed, not confirmed -- a human seals this in nestor ui.

decisions.question: Should human-facing language translation be removed from Nestor, or demoted to an optional add-on -- and what exactly may that touch without breaking the covenant?
decisions.commitment: Demote, do not delete, and only at the presentation layer. Translation stays a working recipe but becomes opt-in (not the desk's default, not a headline door); the desk defaults to decisions. Three layers, decided separately: (A) the presentation/positioning -- the translate recipe, the ('en','es') default, the translation-memory framing -- is demoted (the tractable part, and the one this decision authorizes). (B) the internal source_lang/target_lang naming is left as-is -- it is generic in mechanism (a decision domain already uses the same tag on both sides, nestor/decision.py:69) and renaming it would churn storage, API, tests and docs for near-zero user payoff. (C) the source_text/target_text pair model and the frozen signing contract are NOT touched.
decisions.why: The pivot §4.1/§4.2 already committed to is mostly shipped; what remains is a small, low-risk surface change (the App default domain and the translate recipe's prominence), not surgery. Keeping translation as an add-on rather than deleting it preserves a real working recipe and the negative-control value it has in the bench, while stopping it from mis-signalling the product to a new human. The A/B/C split is the whole point of recording this: it names what is cheap and safe (A), what is not worth it (B), and what is forbidden (C), so a later build cannot drift from 'demote the surface' into 'rip out the model'.
decisions.doors_closed: Deleting the translation recipe (it stays, as an add-on). Renaming source_lang/target_lang internally (out of scope, low payoff, high churn). Touching the (source_norm, target_text, verifier) signing message or the source_text/target_text schema -- every existing seal is signed over those exact bytes (nestor/signing.py:227), so changing them would invalidate the trust root and rebuild the store; that is the generic core, not 'the translation part'. When built, the demotion must move the demo (§4.3) and bench (§4.4) framing with it if either still headlines translation.
